subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` calls fail closed for all legacy session rows that have no `pluginOwnerId`, even though this can stop previously working plugin mutations after upgrade?
rationale: No plugin can safely claim an ownerless row automatically, but rejecting every plugin is an intentional compatibility break at a security and persisted-session boundary that needs maintainer ownership.

options.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
options.body: Reject ownerless rows for plugin-runtime callers, retain operator and non-plugin management, and require deployed behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Add explicit adoption path
options.body: Pause merge until an operator-controlled migration or ownership-adoption workflow is designed and tested for ownerless rows.

options.title: Preserve ownerless access
options.body: Continue allowing plugin-runtime patches on ownerless rows, accepting that any trusted plugin runtime could mutate them.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows for plugin-runtime callers, retain operator and non-plugin management, and require deployed behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work most directly maintains session ownership metadata and mutation behavior in this path.
